methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.intro: This site tracks parties, laws and elections related to policies to reduce immigration in pluralist democracies. This page describes what it actually does: who is included and why, how parties are classified, where the information comes from and how errors are corrected.

scope.title: Scope
scope.text: The site covers pluralist democracies, that is countries whose parliament comes out of elections in which several parties compete, where parties or governments pursue policies to reduce immigration: the 27 member states of the European Union, the United Kingdom, Norway, Switzerland, Iceland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Argentina and Japan. The criterion is political, neither geographic nor ethnic: another country that meets it can be added.
scope.covered: {count} countries in scope currently have at least one party profile. None yet: {missing}.

directory.title: Party directory
directory.criteria: A party is included if it meets one of two conditions: (a) its official programme explicitly calls for reducing or stopping immigration, or for "remigration"; (b) a reference academic dataset classifies it as far right: The PopuList in Europe and, outside Europe, which The PopuList does not cover, ParlGov ("Right-wing" family). A party that meets neither condition is removed, and the removal is recorded in the corrections log.
directory.notJudgment: Including a party means that its position on immigration is documented and sourced. It is neither a judgment on that party nor an endorsement.

basis.parlGov: ParlGov, for countries The PopuList does not cover: {count, plural, one {# party} other {# parties}} ({names})
basis.secondary: Description in an encyclopedia or the press, when no dataset codes the party: {count, plural, one {# party} other {# parties}} ({names})
basis.programme: The party's own programme, as no dataset covers the country: {count, plural, one {# party} other {# parties}} ({names})

grid.title: Classification grid
grid.axis1: Stop / reduce immigration or remigration. The "remigration" tag applies if the party or its leaders explicitly use the term, or if the policy described is substantively equivalent for people residing legally: large-scale, financially encouraged "voluntary" returns, numerical departure targets. Deporting people without legal status, even with a numerical target, counts as reduction. The tag is always sourced, including when the party disputes or rejects the term.
grid.axis2: Programme (the party's commitments, with no adopted text) or concrete measures (an adopted text or a measure in force: a law passed, a decree, an administrative measure). A bill filed but not adopted, or a non-binding resolution, leaves the profile at "programme"; it is mentioned there with its date. A measure is attributed to a party if it was adopted while the party held ministerial posts, or if it is part of a written support agreement the party signed. The "concrete measures" status remains while the measure is in force, whether or not the party is in power; if it is repealed or no longer applied, the profile moves to "concrete measures (historical, repealed on [date])" and keeps a dated history.
grid.registers: To establish that a party has had no text adopted, the profile cites the parliamentary register consulted. When that register could not be consulted, the profile says so instead of drawing a conclusion.

sources.title: Sources
sources.preference: Official sources (parliaments, governments, electoral administrations, the European Union) and academic datasets come first. Where no official source is accessible, the site cites Wikipedia or the press. A party or a campaigning organisation is cited only for its own positions, or as a complement to a neutral source. Figures from a government or a party are attributed to their author.
sources.breakdownIntro: Actual breakdown of the {total} sources cited on the site:
sources.dates: Each source shows the date it was checked and a link to its archived copy in the Wayback Machine. Links are checked and archived every week. A source that could not be verified is marked as such on the page, with the reason: {count, plural, one {# source} other {# sources}} today.

corrections.title: Corrections policy
corrections.text: Every error corrected, every change of classification and every profile removed is recorded in the corrections log, with the date, what the site said, what it says now and the source of the correction. Rewording that changes no fact is not logged.
corrections.report: To report an error, use the contact page. Every report is checked against the sources, whoever sends it.

notDone.title: What this site does not do
notDone.text: It does not feature party youth organisations and publishes no membership or donation link to any party. Non-partisan initiatives (news section) are covered as news: nature, developments, legal status, press coverage, with no profile and no contact or membership link. Its links to external sites carry the "nofollow" attribute: they pass on no search ranking to the parties.

charter.title: Vocabulary charter
charter.intro: The texts on this site describe; they do not characterise. These rules apply to every party profile, election, law and news item:
charter.r1: No dramatising words: no "breakthrough", "earthquake", "spectacular", "crushing", "unprecedented" or "collapse". "Historic" is used only in its literal sense.
charter.r2: "Record", "best" or "worst" result only with the basis of comparison: since when, for which type of election.
charter.r3: Figures from a government, a party or a campaigning organisation are attributed to their author ("according to the Interior Ministry").
charter.r4: Neutral names ("immigration legislation", "return grant"); a party's own vocabulary ("remigration", "invasion") is quoted and attributed.
charter.r5: No judgment on the merits of a programme or a measure: the site reports what a party proposes or gets adopted.
charter.check: The data audit flags these words when they appear outside a quotation.

footer.sources: Sources: official sites, academic datasets (The PopuList, ParlGov), Wikipedia and the press, each dated and archived. Details in the methodology.
footer.notice: Journalistic and documentary content. No personal data is collected for targeting. Every classification is sourced and verifiable — see the methodology.

about.title: About
about.intro: The Migration Policy Watch tracks, with their sources, parties, laws and elections related to policies to reduce immigration in pluralist democracies. It describes what these parties propose and get adopted; it neither supports nor opposes any of them.
about.publisherNamed: The site is published in a personal, non-professional capacity by {name}, publication director.
about.publisherAnonymous: The site is published in a personal, non-professional capacity by an individual whose identity is known to the host, as French law provides. They answer at the address on the contact page.
about.fundingNone: The site has no income: no advertising, no grants, no donations.
about.fundingDonations: The site is funded by donations from its readers, received on Liberapay. Donors have no say over the content. Donations from a party, an elected official or an organisation linked to them are not accepted. The total received is published here every year.
about.independence: No party, movement, campaigning organisation or donor has any say over the content. The site publishes no membership or donation link to any party, and its links to external sites pass on no search ranking. Non-partisan initiatives are covered as news, with no profile.
about.inclusionTitle: What being in the directory means
about.inclusion: A party is in the directory because its position on immigration meets the criteria of the methodology and is documented by sources. It is a judgment neither on that party nor on its voters, and it is not an endorsement.
about.corrections: Errors corrected, changes of classification and removed profiles are recorded in the corrections log, with their date and source. To report an error, write to the address on the contact page.
